title: Presentation & Demo
description: Openings, transitions, and handling Q&A under pressure.

items.scenario: You open a demo of the new incident dashboard for leadership.

choices.text: Um, so yeah, this is a thing we built.
In the next ten minutes I will show how this dashboard cuts mean time to detect from minutes to seconds, then walk through one live incident scenario and take questions.
Let me start with my life story.
Please read the slides; I will stay quiet.

items.explanation: Agenda + outcome + timebox builds executive attention.

items.scenario: The demo environment is slow. Stakeholders are waiting.

choices.text: This always happens; not my fault.
The staging environment is slower than production right now. I will narrate the flow with screenshots while it loads, then switch to the live view for the final step.
Cancel the meeting immediately.
Sit in silence until it works.

items.explanation: Acknowledge, keep value flowing, recover to live when possible.

items.scenario: A VP interrupts: 'Why should we fund this?'

choices.text: Because engineers like shiny tools.

Great question — the business case is fewer prolonged outages. Last quarter we lost an estimated $X in failed checkouts during slow detection. This investment targets that loss with a measurable MTTD reduction.
I will answer later maybe.
Please wait until the end of all thirty slides.

items.explanation: Translate tech into business impact with evidence.

items.scenario: Transition from architecture slide to live demo.

choices.text: Moving on randomly.
That was the design. Now I will show the same flow live: detect anomaly, open runbook, and page the right owner in under a minute.
Forget the architecture; it was wrong.
Any questions on everything at once forever?

items.explanation: Explicit bridge that previews what viewers will see.

items.scenario: Someone asks a question outside the demo scope.

choices.text: That is irrelevant.
Good question — it is adjacent but outside today's scope. I will park it on the parking-lot slide and follow up with a short note after this session so we stay on the detection flow.
Answer for twenty minutes and lose the agenda.
Pretend you did not hear it.

items.explanation: Validate, park, protect the agenda, promise follow-up.

items.scenario: You do not know the answer to a technical question in Q&A.

choices.text: Invent a confident wrong answer.
I do not want to guess on that detail. I will confirm with the owning engineer and send the accurate answer to this group within one business day.
Say nothing and look at your laptop.
Change the topic abruptly.

items.explanation: Honesty + ownership of follow-up beats bluffing.

items.scenario: Close a roadmap presentation to directors.

choices.text: That is all. Bye.

To summarize: three investments, one dependency on platform capacity, and a decision needed on the June canary. I recommend we approve option B today. I will send the one-pager and decision log within an hour.
Any random thoughts?
We will somehow figure it out later.

items.explanation: Summary + decision ask + concrete follow-up artifact.

items.scenario: A skeptical engineer challenges your latency numbers mid-demo.

choices.text: You are wrong and loud.
Appreciate the challenge. These numbers are p95 from last week's production sample — source linked on slide 4. If you have a conflicting dataset, send it after and we will reconcile.
Delete the slide live in panic.
Agree the numbers are fake.

items.explanation: Welcome scrutiny, cite source, offer post-meeting reconciliation.

items.scenario: You are co-presenting and your partner freezes.

choices.text: Wow, awkward.
I can take this section — we are at the rollout plan. After the demo we will cover owners and dates, then open Q&A.
Stare at them until they recover.
End the meeting without notice.

items.explanation: Smoothly take the baton and restate where you are.

items.scenario: Hybrid meeting: remote attendees cannot see your shared screen clearly.

choices.text: Ignore remotes; room matters more.
Remote folks — confirming you can see the dashboard shared window. I will zoom the critical panel and narrate clicks so audio-only participants can follow.
Tell remotes to figure it out.
Stop sharing and only talk.

items.explanation: Check inclusion, adjust visuals, narrate for audio-only.

items.scenario: Product asks you to 'make it exciting' for a customer webinar.

choices.text: Use hype words and hide limitations.
We can keep it customer-exciting and accurate: lead with the outcome they care about, show one crisp workflow, and be explicit about current limits and roadmap timing.
Refuse to present to customers.
Read the internal RFC verbatim.

items.explanation: Excitement without overselling; clarity on limits builds trust.

items.scenario: You have two minutes left and three slides remaining.

choices.text: Speed-read every bullet incomprehensibly.
I will skip the deep-dive slides and land on the decision ask and next steps. Deep-dive appendix is in the leave-behind.
Run overtime without asking.
Abruptly stop mid-sentence.

items.explanation: Protect the decision moment; park detail in appendix.
